angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 736,051 km at 360.73 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.7721 +/- 0.0102 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 360.73 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.058 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Gillon et al. 2013, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-64 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...552A..82G/abstract): 736,051 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.004 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Gillon et al. 2013, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-64 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...552A..82G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5400 +/- 100 K from Gillon et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-64 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...552A..82G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gillon et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-64 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...552A..82G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-64.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.391, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-64 (pscomppars): spectral type G7, from Gillon et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A%26A...552A..82G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-64 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.08 dex, from Gillon et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A%26A...552A..82G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-64 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.022, from Gillon et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A%26A...552A..82G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-64 (pscomppars): age 1.2 Gyr, from Gillon et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A%26A...552A..82G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJ/919/138/table1 (Rot. vel. & per. of hot Jupiter host stars), column Prot: 15.3 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.058 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.972. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.
